family.tagline: Four people, two studies and one Companion Core under one roof.
family.story: Sally runs her consultancy from the front study, and John writes code in the downstairs study, where the Core sits. Steve claims the living-room TV, and Jean has the desk in her room. One Companion Core keeps their files, code, films and homework.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Opens Nextcloud in its own browser and files the client papers Sally lists.
companion.limits: Files only. Sally checks every folder before anything is shared.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Opens Forgejo in its own browser and writes up the issues John lists.
companion.limits: Opens issues only. John reads every issue before it stands.

popup.title: A parcel on the porch
popup.body: A parcel waits on the porch. John carries it through the entry hall and the living room to the study, and Jean holds the door.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Sally lifts the Core out and sets it on the study desk.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: John plugs it in and Steve presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: On her phone, Sally joins the Core's own network, then chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agents and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Sally and John pick OpenClaw. The family names its agents Juniper and Quill. Companion Memory (beta) comes along, and then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Juniper says hello
popup.body: Sally greets Juniper, the agent the family named. Juniper answers, and the Core is running.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Hello, Sally. I am Juniper. Where shall we begin?

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: John codes in his laptop's browser
popup.body: Morning in the study. John works in Code Server, in his laptop's browser. The editor and his projects both sit on the Core.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: John's code lives on his desk
popup.body: John pushes the day's work to Forgejo. The repositories sit on the Core beside him, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: When the notebook breaks, John asks
popup.body: A new idea goes into a JupyterLab notebook first. When it breaks, John asks a model on the Core through Open WebUI, and the chat stays there by default.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: Quill opens the issues John lists
popup.body: After the morning's testing, John lists the bugs he found. Quill opens each one in Forgejo, in its own browser, and John reads every issue before it stands.

say.speaker: john
say.text: The issues are drafted. Please read each before it stands.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: Steve's Steam session runs at home
popup.body: Steve starts a session from the sectional. Steam Headless runs it on the Core and shows it in a browser on the living-room screen.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: Steve signs in to Steam himself
popup.body: Steve signs in with his own Valve account, so the library stays Valve's. The Core runs the session over the home network.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Steve picks the family film
popup.body: It is Friday afternoon, and Steve and Jean argue over the film. Jellyfin plays whichever they pick, from the family's own files on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: The week's dinners, planned once
popup.body: While the kettle boils, Sally plans the week's dinners. Yuvomi keeps the plan and the shopping list in a database on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: Steve ticks off the washing-up
popup.body: It is Steve's night to wash up. He ticks the job off in Yuvomi, the planner Sally used for dinner.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite in your browser

popup.title: Sally writes the quarterly report
popup.body: The quarterly report is due by Thursday. Sally writes it in LibreOffice, in her browser, and the file is saved on the Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: A folder for every client
popup.body: Each client gets a folder in Nextcloud. Sally's contracts sit on the Core, not in a rented drive, and her contacts are served from there too.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Juniper files, Sally checks first
popup.body: A client sends new papers. Juniper opens Nextcloud and files them in the client's folder on the Core. Sally decides what the client sees.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: A search finds last year's invoice
popup.body: Receipts and supplier invoices go through Paperless-ngx on the Core. Every page is read and tagged, so Sally finds an invoice by the words on it.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Contract and schedule, one PDF
popup.body: Sally merges a contract and its schedule into one PDF. Stirling-PDF does the merging on the Core, not on a PDF website.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Jean revises with a quiz
popup.body: Jean keeps her revision notes in Obsidian, as plain files on the Core. A model on the Core quizzes her through Open WebUI, and the chat stays there by default.

beats.capability: serve Wikipedia and other reference sites from the Core

popup.title: No search engine sees Jean's question
popup.body: A geography project is due. Jean looks up glaciers in Kiwix, which serves Wikipedia from the Core, so no search engine sees the question.
popup.note: The Wikipedia file is downloaded once.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Jean checks her homework
popup.body: Before she hands it in, Jean checks her French paragraph in LibreTranslate. It does the work on the Core, so no translation service sees the words.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: John finds the parcel clip
popup.body: John wants to know when the parcel came. Frigate recorded it from the family's drive camera, and the clip sits on the Core.

popup.title: One Core under a stone gable
popup.body: Contracts, code, films and homework. The Brennan household keeps them on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your contracts, code, family films and homework can all sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: study-code uses Code Server, which has no QA screenshot: the owner must list app-qa-screenshot at study-code in content/story/reviewed.json. The writer did not add it.
John's Study has no desk item in the spec (the Core's own desk with the curved monitor is the hero), so John's beats anchor on the core. Sally's beats use desk nth 0 and 1, the two Front Study desks.
Both agents run OpenClaw (casting signature ci-openclaw) and act only in apps on the Core with a web interface; no beat opens an outside website, so the OpenClaw website note is not carried.
Steam Headless beats carry the Valve account, home network and no frame rate, game title or gaming-PC wording. Jean has no agent (casting gives none); Steve has none either.
garden-drive assumes the family owns an IP camera: it is not in the Core box and not in the 3D scene.
Sleeping is never told. Steve and Jean are never shown asleep, and no beat frames the crib or the toddler bed that dress the Kids Room and the Study.
